sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Brings in the test tools, the scheduler, the controller, the database and timeline types, and the reminder enums.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: ReminderService & Scheduler (DaysOfWeek, Timezones & Adherence) (part 1)
sections.title: Fake setup before each test
sections.what: Before each test, builds fake database, queue and timeline objects and a test module that uses them.
sections.why: Likely reason: tests run without a real database or queue.
sections.watch_out: The queue name used for the fake must match the name the scheduler asks for, or the test cannot find it.

sections.name: ReminderService & Scheduler (DaysOfWeek, Timezones & Adherence) (part 2)
sections.title: Day filter and adherence tests
sections.what: Checks that no job is queued when today is not an included day, and that the adherence percentage is worked out correctly from the counts.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are two rules users see directly.
sections.watch_out: The day test uses a day that never matches, so it would still pass if the day check were removed. It does not prove the rule works.

sections.name: ReminderService & Scheduler (DaysOfWeek, Timezones & Adherence) (part 3)
sections.title: Response and snooze tests
sections.what: Checks that a taken dose updates the log with the notes and adds a timeline entry for the medicine. Checks that snooze sets the response to SNOOZED and returns the 15 minute message.
sections.why: Likely reason: these guard how responses are saved and shown in history.
sections.watch_out: The snooze test checks the message and the stored value only. It does not show that a reminder comes back after 15 minutes, because nothing tested does that.

summary: Automated tests for the reminder scheduler and reminder controller, using fake database, queue and timeline objects.
purpose: Checks several reminder rules so that changes do not quietly break them.
why: Likely reason: protects the adherence math and response recording, which users see directly.
how: Builds a small test module with fake database, queue and timeline objects before each test, then checks a day filter, the adherence percentage, a taken dose with its timeline entry, and snooze.
inputs: Test data defined inside the file.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner.
risks: Some test names promise coverage that does not exist, such as timezones. The day filter test passes for a reason unrelated to the rule, so it does not prove the rule works. Queuing, water and meal paths, deletion and the share routes are not tested here.
debug: Run the reminder tests and read which check failed. If a fake is missing a function, the error names it. Make sure fakes match what the code calls.
